about: Every 'chain checks' clause of every story in M1-STORIES.md, split into atomic claims and reconciled with the Lean. class: guard (the Lean decides it), omission (the Lean does not model it; the simulator says so), overrule (the Lean decides differently; the simulator follows the Lean). A guard or overrule row is one claim of one kind — guard (a hypothesis the transition requires), refusal (the clause states a refusal), payment (a flow field pays it), post-state (the resulting state, optionally 'updates': the only datum fields the post-state sets), no-guard (the constructor has no hypothesis), verdict (a conjunct of consumableState) — and names the Lean declaration (decl: a Step constructor, consumableState, SysStep.register, Trace.cons or a theorem), the hypothesis for a guard or refusal (hyp), the exact text that entails the claim (text), and exactly one semantic tie: reason (a refusal name, which the core's LEAN_GUARDS binds to the constructor and binder that refuse it; a refusal claim also needs a step of its story refused for it), verdict (bound to its conjunct), or match (a step of the story's own scenario, whose constructor is derived from the record; a payment claim's step must pay through the named field; an untouched-except claim's step must change only the listed fields). The scenario gate parses each constructor into its hypotheses, flow record and post-state and requires the text inside the part the kind names; it fails on an unclassified fragment, a clause absent from its story, a text outside its part, a tie the declaration does not decide, and a Step guard hypothesis no refusal name claims.

clauses.note: Step.register carries no inception and no validation predicate; the registrant's bytes are not modelled. The Env has no predicate for it either.

clauses.clause: the AID is absent from the registry

clauses.note: Sys.set moves the leaf with the state (State.leaf); SysStep.other leaves the registry alone for rotate, poison, freeze and top-up (T8_edges_leave_the_leaf).

clauses.clause: this is the only way the token can ever be minted
clauses.note: registration is the only SysStep that touches the registry, and it needs the AID absent from it; every non-absent AID is registered (T8_present_implies_registered), so a second minting is refused for the rest of the AID's life.
the registration flow brings exactly D and B; a transaction bringing less is not a Step at all.

clauses.clause: signatures at the current threshold over the rotation bytes
clauses.note: one predicate stands for the three cryptographic checks of the advance (Env.rotationTo doc); the same hev guards every rotate constructor and the freeze.

receipts from at least `toad` of the new witness set
Then it pays `P` from the pool to Hal
clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }
clauses.note: paid when the pool covers P (hpay : p.P ≤ l.pool); otherwise the rotation lands unpaid (Step.rotateKeepUnpaid, hnopay): payment is never a gate.

clauses.clause: exactly the advance predicate on the presented rotation
that the checkpoint is not poisoned

clauses.note: the rationale of the modelling assumption stated on Step.freeze's doc comment (no freeze from a poisoned state); the Lean has the guard hclean, not the reason for it.

clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, b := p.B }
clauses.note: the freeze also needs the bond present (hb : l.b = p.B; refusal freeze-bond-missing), which the story states only as its 'after'.
Live is the datum plus the value held; the freeze sets only b (the freeze bond, value) and leaves sn, epoch, poisoned, bornAt, refundTo, dreg and pool as they were — the old keys stay.

clauses.clause: that both bonds are full on the output
clauses.note: the depositing rotation's output holds exactly D and B; the guards hd / hb refuse a datum already above full (bond-over-full).

clauses.clause: then it pays `D_reg + B + pool` to the refund address
clauses.text: refund := some { addr := refund'.getD l.refundTo, dreg := l.dreg, b := l.b, pool := l.pool }

clauses.clause: both bonds full on the output
one stolen member key of a multisig cannot poison
clauses.note: the threshold itself is inside Env.quorum; a single member key is not modelled.

clauses.clause: that the epoch is not already poisoned
the signature over the new address at the new threshold by the keys the rotation reveals
A relayer submitting her public rotation without that signature leaves the address unchanged
clauses.note: a rotation that names an address the new keys did not sign in the intent message is refused whole (hauth fails), not landed with the old address; a rotation naming no address needs no signature and keeps it. Story 8's scenario plays both (D-032, D-038).

clauses.clause: the second rotation is at the tip's sequence
reveals the same keys the tip holds
clauses.note: one predicate stands for the whole duplicity check (Env.duplicityAt doc).

clauses.clause: is signed at the current threshold
carries receipts from at least `toad` of the tip's witnesses
and differs from the accepted one
No history needed: the revealed keys are the current keys
clauses.note: the model has no key material; the epoch counter stands for the current keys, and duplicityAt is asked at (epoch, sn) only.
D-036: a close is a witnessed rotation by the next keys, not a signature by the current ones; Mallory with the current keys is refused no-witnessed-rotation.
D-036: a close lands poisoned or not; what it needs is the new keys' signed close intent (D-038), which a relayer with the public rotation does not have.

clauses.clause: Then it pays everything to the refund address
clauses.text: refund := some { addr := refund'.getD l.refundTo, dreg := l.dreg, b := l.b, pool := l.pool }

clauses.note: the tombstone keeps the epoch the closing rotation opened and its sequence; not terminal (D-036): a later witnessed rotation reopens it.

clauses.clause: the signature on the payment satisfies the current threshold
clauses.note: the consumer's own threshold check on its transaction is outside this machine (consumableState doc).
validity (D-027, A11) is reserved in the datum and not modelled (Checkpoint.lean module doc).
every non-present state is False; each present failure names its conjunct (story 11's scenario walks all seven).

clauses.clause: the checkpoint is juvenile for `W` slots
anyone can advance it onward with Alice's later public rotations
clauses.note: the submitter is not modelled. Action.actor derives the authorizer from the action and a rotation's is nextKeys — Alice's rotation authorizes itself; nothing in Step or SysStep names who carries the transaction. Scenario 12 plays Hal landing Alice's later rotation, which the Lean admits because the evidence (hev) holds, not because 'anyone' is a rule of the machine. Campaign 1 anchored this to `| .register .. => .anyone`, the actor of a registration: an over-attribution.

clauses.clause: the moment that happens, Mallory's bonds answer to Alice's keys (story 8)
clauses.note: the bonds answer to whoever can move the refund address: after Alice's rotation only her new keys can sign a new one in the intent message (hauth, D-038), and close and withdrawal pay there (Step.close, Step.rotateWithdraw).

clauses.clause: It can happen once per AID, ever
clauses.note: for one AID the state guard (present / closed / convicted) refuses first (already-present, as scenario 12 plays it); the leaf guard is the system-level reason, exercised by the gate's multi-AID generator.
only the pool (value) moves; sn, epoch, poisoned, bornAt, refundTo, dreg and b stay — juvenility is not restarted.
the constructor has no guard hypothesis: no evidence, no signature.
hunters, watchers and timing are not modelled; evidence is a table.

clauses.text: hunter := some { addr := payee, pool := p.P }
clauses.note: no UTxO in the model: 'first' is whichever rotation the machine sees first; it lands paid.

clauses.clause: the second fails on the spent input
clauses.note: no UTxO in the model: the second advance fails because the state moved and its evidence no longer matches (no-witnessed-rotation).

her checkpoint stays consumable as long as it is bonded
clauses.note: consumableState has no upper bound on age; bonded means both conjuncts l.dreg = p.D and l.b = p.B (next row).

A missing rotation is what a freeze (story 3) makes visible, not what the consumer sees. Campaign 1 anchored this to the juvenility conjunct: an over-attribution.

clauses.clause: Nothing on chain says she is gone
clauses.note: no age, no liveness signal in the datum; consumableState reads bornAt only for juvenility.

a withdraw rotation from a live state pays D + B + pool to the refund address

the next keys can close a paused checkpoint: zero paid, token burned

a paused checkpoint cannot be frozen: no freeze bond to take

no duplicity proof, no conviction

nothing but a reopen leaves Closed
